home.subtitle: Here's how to get the most out of Yarnboard.
home.stitchFiddleDescription: Save a stitchfiddle.com share link, then import it with one click. Yarnboard turns the chart into a colored grid you can view alongside a plain color-key list -- no written instructions, since that's a premium Stitch Fiddle feature, but you can always add your own via the pattern's Edit page afterwards.
home.submitTitle: Submit a pattern from a URL or PDF
home.submitDescription: Paste a link to a pattern page and Yarnboard scrapes the materials, abbreviations, and instructions automatically. If a site blocks automatic fetching, or the pattern only exists as a PDF (e.g. a paid Etsy/Ravelry download), upload the saved page or PDF instead. Either way, you review and can edit everything before it's published.
home.useDescription: Browse everything the community has published, save the ones you want to come back to, and check off each instruction step as you work -- your progress is tracked per pattern, just for you.
home.editDescription: Fix a typo, update materials, or add missing steps on any pattern you submitted, from My Uploads. Heads up: editing a pattern's instructions resets everyone's checklist progress on it, since the steps may no longer line up.

submit.title: Submit a Pattern
submit.intro: Paste a link to a knitting or crochet pattern webpage. We'll pull out the title, materials, abbreviations, and instructions for you to review before publishing.

submit.uploadFallbackIntro: Couldn't fetch that page automatically -- some sites block automated requests. If you have the page saved as an HTML file (open it in your browser, then "Save Page As..." / "Save As" and choose "Webpage, HTML only"), or the pattern as a PDF (e.g. a paid pattern from Etsy/Ravelry), you can upload it here instead. The URL above is still used to credit the original source and to avoid duplicates.

stitchFiddle.title: Stitch Fiddle Charts
stitchFiddle.intro: Paste a link to one of your public Stitch Fiddle charts. Import turns it into a pattern with a reconstructed chart image and a color list -- written instructions aren't generated (that's a Stitch Fiddle premium feature), so add those yourself afterward via the pattern's Edit page if you want them.
